answer: Julius Caesar received twenty-three stab wounds when he was assassinated.
quote: Thus informed, he was stabbed with twenty-three wounds, uttering not a word, though some have written that as Marcus Brutus rushed at him, he said in Greek, 'You too, my child?'

answer: As Julius Caesar was about to cross the Rubicon, he paused and said, 'Let us go where the omens of the Gods and the iniquity of our enemies call us. The die is cast.'
quote: Eamus... quo deorum ostenta et inimicorum iniquitas vocat. Iacta alea est.

answer: Augustus boasted that he found it built of brick, but left it clothed in marble.
quote: that he had found it built of brick, but left it clothed in marble

answer: After the defeat of Varus, Augustus was so deeply affected that he let the hair of his head and beard grow for months, and sometimes hit his head against a door, crying out, 'Quintilius Varus, give me back my legions!'
quote: Quintili Vare, legiones redde!

answer: On his deathbed, Augustus asked his friends if they thought he had played his part in the comedy of life suitably, adding a common theatrical closing line: "If all has been well given, clap your hands, and all with mirth dismiss us."
quote: Did he not seem to you to have played his part in life's comedy Suitably? ... If all has been well given, clap your hands, And all with mirth dismiss us.

answer: Caligula planned to appoint his horse, Incitatus, to the consulship.
quote: He planned even to make his horse Incitatus consul.

answer: Claudius was found hiding in a dark room behind the curtains of a door.
quote: Terrified at the news of the murder, he had stolen away to a neighbouring balcony and hid himself among the hangings of a door.

answer: As he prepared to die, Nero repeatedly exclaimed what an artist was dying in him.
quote: Qualis artifex pereo!

answer: Feeling the approach of death, Vespasian joked that he must be becoming a god, as his last words were 'Vae, puto, deus fio' (Woe is me. Methinks I am turning into a god).
quote: Vae, puto, deus fio.

answer: Titus uttered the memorable remark, 'Friends, I have lost a day,' on a night during dinner when he remembered that he had done no one a favour during the entire day.
quote: Friends, I have lost a day.

answer: The young Caesar was captured by pirates near the island of Pharmacusa.
quote: While he was waiting for the fleet after paying the money, he immediately manned some ships from that very island, set out in pursuit of the pirates as they were leaving, and captured them.

answer: Julius Caesar tried to hide his baldness by combing his sparse hair forward from the crown of his head.
quote: His baldness was a disfigurement which troubled him not a little... and so he used to comb forward his scant locks from the crown of his head.

answer: Augustus used the phrase "faster than cooked asparagus" to mean something done very quickly.
quote: citius quam asparagi cocuntur

answer: Augustus had deposited his will with the Vestal Virgins.
quote: His will was deposited with the Vestal Virgins, to whom he had delivered three rolls, sealed up, nearly a year before he died at Nola...

answer: Tiberius possessed such extraordinary finger strength that he could flick a fresh, sound apple with his finger and pierce it, and he could also break a boy's head, or at least scratch it severely, with a flick of his finger.
quote: His physical frame was vigorous and of more than ordinary size... His physical strength was indeed so great that he could pierce a fresh, sound apple with his finger, and crack a boy's head, or at least a hard skull, with a flick of his finger.

answer: Tiberius had the fisherman's face scrubbed with the huge mullet because the man had climbed up to him on a rugged and inaccessible crag by a secret path to present the fish.
quote: he ordered the man's face to be scrubbed with the mullet

answer: Caligula slept very little, not more than three hours a night.
quote: He was little given to sleep, for he never rested more than three hours at night

answer: Claudius added three new letters to the Latin alphabet, which he introduced during his censorship.
quote: He also added three new letters to the alphabet, maintaining that they were greatly needed and updating the previous rules.

answer: When his Golden House was finished, Nero merely remarked that at last he was beginning to live like a human being.
quote: that he was at last beginning to live like a human being

answer: When Augustus was a boy and Galba came to pay his respects, Augustus pinched his cheek and said, 'You too, child, will taste a morsel of my power.'
quote: Et tu quoque, fili, gustabis imperii nostri.

answer: Otho shaved every day and smeared his face with moist bread, a practice which he began when down first appeared on his cheeks in order that he might never grow a beard.
quote: He is even said to have shaved every day and to have smeared his face with moist bread, a practice which he began when down first appeared on his cheeks in order that he might never grow a beard.

answer: Vitellius called his enormous dish of rare and costly ingredients the "Shield of Minerva."
quote: He also made a new dish of extraordinary size, which he dubbed the 'Shield of Minerva, city-guardian.' In it he mixed the livers of pike, the brains of pheasants and peacocks, the tongues of flamingoes, and the milt of lampreys

answer: Early in his reign, Domitian used to spend an hour alone in private every day, during which time he would catch flies and stab them with a sharply-pointed stylus.
quote: At the beginning of his reign he used to spend hours in seclusion every day, doing nothing but catch flies and stab them with a terribly sharp stylus.

answer: Domitian began his official letters with the phrase, "Our Lord and God would have it so."
quote: Our Lord and God would have it so

answer: When Titus became emperor, he dismissed Queen Berenice from Rome immediately, sending her away against her own and his desires.
quote: Berenice he sent away from Rome at once, against her will and his own.

answer: The Lives of the Twelve Caesars by Suetonius does not cover the reign or actions of Hadrian, as it ends with Domitian.
